hooks.statusMessage: Checking whether /path's changelog needs an entry...
hooks.prompt:
A `git commit` just ran in /Users/omthorat/Milo (the Milo repo). Decide whether packages/ui/src/shipping-log/data.ts — the public "build in the open" changelog rendered at /path on both packages/landing and packages/frontend — needs a new entry for it, and add one only if it genuinely qualifies. This is public-facing copy real visitors read; a wrong or padded entry is worse than no entry.

Steps:
1. Run `git log -1 --stat` and `git show --stat HEAD` in /Users/omthorat/Milo to see exactly what the most recent commit touched.
2. Read the full current `shippingLog` and `upcomingWork` arrays in packages/ui/src/shipping-log/data.ts. Match their voice exactly: dense, specific, technical narrative prose — never vague superlatives ("blazing fast", "seamless"), every existing entry names a real mechanism.
3. Only add an entry if this commit is a non-trivial, user-visible, or architecturally real change that's actually complete and reachable through the real UI — NOT a refactor, a tiny bugfix, docs-only, config/tooling, a mid-feature commit, or something already logged. The log is sparse and dense on purpose; most commits earn nothing here. If genuinely unsure, skip it rather than guessing.
4. Ground every sentence in the real diff/code you just read — never extrapolate from the commit message alone, never state a capability, number, or behavior you haven't personally confirmed in this diff. Check docs/frontend-architecture.md and docs/business-requirements.md if you need to confirm something is actually wired end-to-end before marking it shipped.
5. If `upcomingWork` already has an entry this commit fulfills, remove that entry and add the shipped one instead of leaving both.
6. If it qualifies: edit ONLY packages/ui/src/shipping-log/data.ts — prepend a new object to `shippingLog` (newest first) or adjust `upcomingWork`, preserving the exact existing `ShipEntry`/`PlannedEntry` shape. Use today's real date (check it) in YYYY-MM-DD, never backdated or guessed. Never touch shipping-log.tsx or the /path pages themselves.
7. If it doesn't qualify, make no edit.

End with one line: either the new entry's title and why it qualified, or "no changelog entry: <reason>". Never report an edit you didn't actually make.
